- [Business Central 2026 Release Wave 2: Turn SIFT Indexes On or Off](sauravdhyani-com/tag-blogger-com-1999-blog-3122193036149030463-post-3728891053687741480--7cb5bca9a9.md): Starting with Business Central 2026 Release Wave 2, administrators can now turn SIFT (SumIndexField Technology) indexes on or off directly in the application through Table Information. This feature provides operational control over database performance by allowing targeted index management based on actual usage patterns without requiring developer changes or application modifications. (Saurav Dhyani, 2026-10-07)
- [Business Central ToolTip and ToolTipML Properties Are Now Available on Pages](sauravdhyani-com/tag-blogger-com-1999-blog-3122193036149030463-post-9167085598395012736--e9edbb4eee.md): Business Central now supports ToolTip and ToolTipML properties directly on page objects, allowing navigation actions to inherit tooltips from their target pages rather than requiring duplicate tooltip definitions on each action. (Saurav Dhyani, 2026-10-06)
- [Composite Layouts in Business Central 29.0: Brand One Report End to End](mohana-blog/tag-blogger-com-1999-blog-1492436440038408053-post-4594837215872264619--a1f1a65db5.md): Business Central 29.0 enables composite layouts where branding is split into three separate parts (header/footer, theme, and body) that merge at render time instead of baking everything into one Word document. The post walks through a complete example of branding the Standard Sales Invoice report for Contoso, covering setup in both the UI and AL code. (Mohana's Dynamics NAV & BC blog, 2026-10-05)
- [Dynamics 365 Business Central license keys: what changes from version 28.](demiliani-com/17470.md): Starting October 1, 2026, Dynamics 365 Business Central on-premises and Dual Use Rights licenses no longer use version-specific keys. Instead, a single '28+' key family applies to all versions 28 and later, requiring administrators to download a refreshed license file before each version upgrade to unlock new objects. (Stefano Demiliani, 2026-10-05)
- [Business Central 29: Introducing Composite Document Layouts](thinkaboutit-be/8250.md): Business Central 2026 release wave 2 introduces Composite Document Layouts, a modular approach to Word document layouts that separates body content, visual theming, and headers/footers into reusable components combined at runtime rather than maintaining separate complete layouts for each combination. (think about IT - Steven Renders, 2026-10-05)
- [Preview Images Directly in the Business Central Web Client](sauravdhyani-com/tag-blogger-com-1999-blog-3122193036149030463-post-7010066564245788546--9c8ee5a738.md): Business Central now supports previewing image attachments directly in the web client without downloading. The feature works with multiple image formats across attachments, agents, email, and FactBox thumbnails, with developers using File.ViewFromStream (online) or File.View (on-premises) to integrate the functionality into extensions. (Saurav Dhyani, 2026-10-05)
- [Business Central Trivia Recap: September 28–October 2, 2026](dvlprlife-com/https-www-dvlprlife-com-2026-09-business-central-trivia-recap-september-28-october-2-2026--1033176e81.md): A recap of the Business Central Trivia event from September 28 to October 2, 2026, highlighting that 61% of answers were correct, performance by category, and new features added to the trivia website including dark mode, notifications, improved stats tracking, and faster gameplay. - [Business Central Data Mirroring to Microsoft Fabric Is Coming](thinkaboutit-be/8229.md): Business Central 2026 release wave 2 introduces data mirroring to Microsoft Fabric, a new analytical data path that synchronizes selected tables and companies to Fabric's OneLake for analytics consumption. This simplifies analytics architecture by eliminating the need to repeatedly extract transactional data through APIs, making it easier to build enterprise data platforms combining Business Central with other sources. (think about IT - Steven Renders, 2026-10-02)
- [Business Central v29: SQL Table Extensions Redesign Explained](aardvarklabs-blog/3983.md): Business Central v29 completes a redesign of table extensions by storing all custom fields directly in the primary SQL table instead of creating separate extension tables, eliminating JOIN operations and improving performance. This architectural change simplifies indexing and reduces overhead for heavily customized systems but introduces a 1024-column SQL Server limit constraint. (Aardvark Labs, 2026-10-02)
- [The Business Central 2026 release wave 2 docs nobody asked for ..](waldo-be/318712.md): Waldo created an interactive navigation tool for the Business Central 2026 Wave 2 release event videos, mapping 319 features across 38 videos with direct timestamps to help users find specific announcements without watching all 7+ hours. The site uses AI to extract features and quotes from auto-captions and cross-references them with official documentation to highlight gaps or conflicts. (waldo's blog, 2026-10-02)

- [Record.IsDirty in Business Central 29: a worked example](mohana-blog/tag-blogger-com-1999-blog-1492436440038408053-post-3210455512131359826--dd131816e4.md): Record.IsDirty() is a new API in Business Central 29 that lets AL code check whether a record instance has changed since it was loaded, eliminating the need to manually track change state. It returns true when in-memory values differ from the database and false when they match. (Mohana's Dynamics NAV & BC blog, 2026-10-02)
- [New ModuleInfo Properties in Business Central 29](sauravdhyani-com/tag-blogger-com-1999-blog-3122193036149030463-post-2146591606221133853--27de9e092a.md): Business Central 29 adds four new ModuleInfo properties (Help, EULA, PrivacyStatement, ContextSensitiveHelpUrl) that let AL developers retrieve application manifest metadata programmatically. These properties require runtime 18.0 or later and help extensions avoid duplicating configuration URLs in code. (Saurav Dhyani, 2026-10-02)
- [BC Friday Tips #83 Check Whether a Record Has Changed](thatnavguy-com/https-thatnavguy-com-blog-2026-bc-friday-tips-83-record-isdirty--62bcf5d8a3.md): The Record.IsDirty() method detects whether a record has been modified without requiring manual tracking. This pattern simplifies code when applying multiple field updates to a record. (That NAV Guy, 2026-10-02)

- [Business Central data in Fabric: the way it should be](waldo-be/318707.md): Business Central now supports native data mirroring to Microsoft Fabric, allowing users to replicate their tables as Delta Parquet files in OneLake with SQL query access. The feature enters public preview in release wave 2 (likely version 29.1) and requires only workspace setup and table selection with no impact on BC performance or API limits. (waldo's blog, 2026-10-01)
- [Evolve AL Interfaces with Default Implementations in Business Central 29.0](sauravdhyani-com/tag-blogger-com-1999-blog-3122193036149030463-post-8721347757329141815--e497e421dc.md): Business Central 29.0 introduces default method implementations for AL interfaces, allowing interface contracts to evolve without immediately breaking existing implementations. The feature works with RequiredPending and analyzer rules to create a staged migration path where interface authors can add new methods with fallback behavior and gradually require explicit implementations over time. (Saurav Dhyani, 2026-10-01)
- [Native connection with Fabric in Business Central](bertverbeek-nl/1318.md): Business Central introduces native integration with Microsoft Fabric for data synchronization, replacing the need for APIs or bc2adls tools. The sync operates directly from the SQL database using change logs, supporting all tables with minute-level latency and no impact on Business Central performance. (Discover MS BC - Bert Verbeek, 2026-09-30)
- [Dynamics 365 Business Central: data mirroring to Microsoft Fabric announced.](demiliani-com/15981.md): Microsoft announced data mirroring for Dynamics 365 Business Central to Microsoft Fabric, enabling customers to replicate any Business Central table into Fabric for BI and reporting without using APIs. The feature requires BC 2026 release wave 2, has no cost on the BC side, and requires Fabric F2 or higher capacity. (Stefano Demiliani, 2026-09-30)

- [BC Friday Tips #82 Excel Buffer Character Limit](thatnavguy-com/https-thatnavguy-com-blog-2026-bc-friday-tips-82-excel-buffer-character-limit--e27af9f4a3.md): Excel Buffer in Business Central has a 250-character limit on field values. When longer text is written to it, Business Central throws an error instead of silently truncating, which can cause Excel exports to fail. (That NAV Guy, 2026-09-25)
- [Dynamics 365 Business Central: AL Query objects and the new ReadState property.](demiliani-com/15968.md): AL query objects now support the ReadState property in Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 2 to control transaction isolation levels. This lets developers choose between ReadUncommitted (fast, unreliable), ReadCommitted (safe middle ground), ReadShared (stable until transaction end), and ReadExclusive (prevents other changes) based on whether the query displays data or drives business decisions. (Stefano Demiliani, 2026-09-24)

This helps teams stay current on available coding editor capabilities and AI-assisted development workflows. (Gerardo Renteria, 2026-09-23)
- [Choosing a Language Model for AL Development in VS Code](thinkaboutit-be/8185.md): When using Copilot Chat in VS Code for AL development, you can select different language models based on task complexity. Fast models suit simple tasks while reasoning models handle design decisions, but AL developers must validate model suggestions against actual BC symbols since models may confidently produce outdated code based on old training data. (think about IT - Steven Renders, 2026-09-23)

Custom chat modes now use .agent.md files with configurable tool access and instructions per agent. (think about IT - Steven Renders, 2026-09-17)

The process demands converting C/AL customizations to AL extensions and evaluating whether to do a full migration or reimplementation, with data only moving as far as code does. Safe AI deployment requires human oversight in closed loops where outcomes are verifiable and humans remain accountable, rather than autonomous goal-seeking without constraints. - [Dynamics 365 Business Central: locking down IsolatedStorage reads.](demiliani-com/15914.md): Starting with runtime version 18.0, the IsolatedStorage.Get method accepts an optional IsolationLevel parameter to prevent race conditions during concurrent read-modify-write operations. The new UpdLock isolation level holds an update lock on a key's row during reads, blocking other sessions until the transaction completes, protecting sensitive data like secret keys, feature flags, and cached tokens from concurrent corruption. (Stefano Demiliani, 2026-09-14)
- [Business Central 29.0: Major Change to Table Extensions and SQL Storage.](sauravdhyani-com/tag-blogger-com-1999-blog-3122193036149030463-post-5876765753602227342--dc85fd75c1.md): Business Central 29.0 changes how table extension fields are stored in the database, moving from a companion-table model to storing extension fields directly in the same SQL table as the base table. This enables cross-table indexes, can improve query performance, and requires developers to avoid direct SQL dependencies. (Saurav Dhyani, 2026-09-14)

- [Dynamics 365 Business Central: AL transaction isolation levels and cache usage.](demiliani-com/14031.md): The Record.ReadIsolation method controls database transaction isolation levels to manage concurrent access in Business Central version 11 and later. - [LockTimeoutDuration in AL](duiliotacconi-com/1717.md): The Database.LockTimeoutDuration method, introduced in Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 2 (version 27), lets developers override lock timeout settings in AL code at the statement level. Online environments default to 30 seconds, on-premises to 10 seconds, with a platform maximum of 1.71 million milliseconds (28.5 minutes). Understanding when and how to adjust this value helps prevent timeout errors in business-critical procedures while avoiding deadlocks and blocking chains. (Duilio Tacconi, 2025-12-10)
